title: A Echo for the Colony
premise: Silas Brightwater, a xenolinguist haunted by dreams that arrive in no human tongue, pilots the long-haul freighter Echo's Wake across a system of worlds that have gone linguistically silent since the fleet's occupation. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, Silas realizes it was a message—one encoded in the grammar of the extinct colony language they alone can still read. Hunted by a fleet that wants the signal buried and aided by a stowaway archivist named Vey, Silas races to the relay at the edge of dead space to rebroadcast the colony's last testimony before the fleet's truce expires and silence becomes permanent. At the relay, Silas must choose between destroying their own ship to send the echo or letting the dead stay quiet; they send it, and the system's worlds begin, haltingly, to speak again.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa is a former shipping-route dispatcher who spent a decade listening to pilots' logs from the outer colonies before turning to fiction. She writes about language, distance, and the people who carry messages no one asked for.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Silas Brightwater, mid-haul on the Echo's Wake, experiences the nine-second gravity flicker and hears, in the ship's groaning hull, something that sounds like syntax. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in a carefully maintained invisibility.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: A portrait of Silas's routine: delivering cargo to colony worlds that no longer answer in their own tongues, trading in dead languages, dreaming each night in a grammar no human uses. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: What the Hull Remembered
chapters.summary: Silas decodes the flicker's pattern from the ship's sensor logs and finds it matches the cadence of Kessari, the extinct colony language they were raised on. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread and longing tangled together.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Silas discovers Vey, a young archivist hiding in a cargo pod, who carries a stolen fragment of the fleet's sealed colony records—and who recognized the flicker too. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two people who shouldn't exist to each other.

chapters.title: Port of Quiet
chapters.summary: Docking at Meridian Reach, Silas sees fleet censors scrubbing language archives and realizes the nine-second event was no accident of physics. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the slow collapse of the belief that staying invisible is possible.

chapters.title: Vey's Testimony
chapters.summary: Vey reveals the fleet's truce with the colony worlds expires in forty days, after which all native-language records will be destroyed under the Silence Accord. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: fear converted into purpose.

chapters.title: Grammar of the Dead
chapters.summary: Working through the night, Silas and Vey translate the flicker: it is a fragment of the colony's final broadcast, truncated mid-sentence, pointing toward the relay at the edge of dead space. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Ear
chapters.summary: A fleet listening post pings the Echo's Wake; Silas performs a flawless routine inspection while Vey hides the records in the ship's linguistic core. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror managed through performance.

chapters.title: Dreams Without Translation
chapters.summary: Silas's dreams intensify—full sentences in Kessari now, addressed to them by name—and they confess to Vey that the language may be living in them somehow. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the frightening intimacy of being chosen by something lost.

chapters.title: Burned at Halcyon Drift
chapters.summary: At a refueling station, a fleet informant flags Silas's name; they barely escape, but the ship's transponder is burned and the route is now a hunt. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: guilt—Vey believes she brought the danger.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Silence
chapters.summary: They seek out Odile Ferran, a disgraced fleet cartographer living off-grid, who knows the dead-space relay's approach corridors—and who once signed the Silence Accord. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: an old woman's shame meeting a chance at amendment.

chapters.title: Into Dead Space
chapters.summary: The Echo's Wake leaves charted space with no beacons, no rescue window, following Odile's hand-drawn corridor maps while fleet pursuit ships shadow the boundary. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: commitment—there is no route back that isn't surrender.

chapters.title: The Corridor That Listens
chapters.summary: In dead space the ship's systems begin echoing Kessari phonemes back at them; Vey theorizes the relay itself has been storing the colony's broadcast for decades. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency—the signal is dying.

chapters.title: What Odile Signed
chapters.summary: Odile confesses she helped design the Silence Accord's archive purges and offers the one thing that can authenticate the relay broadcast: her original command cipher. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: justice demanded of oneself, not granted by law.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: A fleet cutter crosses into dead space to intercept them; Silas threads the Echo's Wake through a gravity shear, losing the cargo bay and nearly losing Vey. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the cost of the race made physical and irreversble.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: With six days left, they calculate the relay's remaining power: it can broadcast the colony's full testimony exactly once, and only if someone speaks the activation phrase in living Kessari. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: the weight of being the only voice left.

chapters.title: Silas Answers
chapters.summary: Silas realizes the dreams were never haunting but rehearsal—the colony language has been teaching itself to them, preparing a speaker. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: belonging found not among people but in a language that refused to die.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They reach the ancient relay, half-ruined, still holding the colony's final testimony in its memory core—and find a fleet boarding team already docked, waiting under truce law. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the race arriving at its narrowest point.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Spoken
chapters.summary: In the boarding team's nine-second comms blackout—the fleet's own gravity-flicker test—Silas speaks the activation phrase, and the relay begins to sing the colony's testimony across every open band. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: climax—the dead given their voice at last.

chapters.title: What the System Heard
chapters.summary: Across the occupied worlds, people hear the colony's last broadcast; the truce collapses not into war but into hearings, as the Silence Accord's signatories are named—including Odile, who surrenders herself voluntarily. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: justice arriving outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Answer
chapters.summary: Facing a system that now remembers aloud, the fleet command withdraws the purge order rather than enforce it; Vey is granted archive amnesty, and the Echo's Wake is officially listed as lost. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: survival without vindication, and peace with that.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Kessari
chapters.summary: Silas takes the long route again, but now colony worlds answer in their own tongues, and at night the dreams have quieted into something like conversation. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging is not a place but a voice answered.
